episode_title: Learnings From AI on the Volcano

real_qa.q: What does agentic shift mean for product design and workflow reimagining in organizations?
real_qa.r: The agentic shift is significant and probably more than other AI changes this year. Product is no longer a tool, so workflow has to be reimagined across different business units where you are not responding but it's much more integrated. Tools that are built for one box on the org chart lose their boundaries.

real_qa.q: Why is verification becoming a critical bottleneck in AI agent systems?
real_qa.r: Generating outputs is now becoming relatively cheap, but checking it is not. Someone needs to review what agents produce. In regulated sectors especially, we do need to keep critical human verification and validation of what is then going into systems in production.

real_qa.q: What is the difference between hierarchical and horizontal organizational models when managing multiple AI agents?
real_qa.r: If you run thirty agents on a single project or multiple projects, that person becomes a bottleneck. The question is whether the human is in a consulting mind like a senior partner with final say, or if the organization becomes one with a series of very senior people, so less hierarchical and much more flat horizontal.

real_qa.q: How should physical AI approaches combine with traditional hybrid methods in industrial applications?
real_qa.r: Whether it's for physical AI or other approaches, the notion of hybrid beating just a single approach was something that came up. When we talk about physical AI, it's around how do we build and train models and what do those models learn from. This goes back to human plus AI unless having systems run constantly autonomously.
real_qa.requete: physical AI hybrid approach industrial applications

real_qa.q: Why are organizational change management and user adoption still critical in AI implementation despite technical advances?
real_qa.r: It came up as relatively novel that we have to account for people and change management and user adoption. Having been doing this for fifteen years, this has always been one of the critical components. I don't think I've ever had a conversation about AI without talking about the business and value that's generated.
real_qa.requete: change management user adoption AI implementation
